description: β numerical validation — Monte Carlo check of the analytical variance formula for the octonion associator, Fano-triple case. Setup (per docs/research/variance_of_associator.md § "Worked example:
comments: β numerical validation — Monte Carlo check of the analytical variance
formula for the octonion associator, Fano-triple case.
Setup (per docs/research/variance_of_associator.md § "Worked example:
single Fano generator"):
A(a, b, c) := ‖[a, b, c]‖²   where [a,b,c] = (a·b)·c − a·(b·c)
Unperturbed: [a,b,c] = 2·e_7, A = 4.
Perturb a_1 → 1 + δ, δ ~ N(0, σ²). The analytical first-order GUM
variance (from the β document, derivation):
Var(A) ≈ 64 σ²                                (TRUTH)
If the current compiler's stepwise scalar-product rule were applied
instead, it would give:
Var_compiler(A) ≈ 16 σ²                       (COMPILER, 4× low)
This test computes the sample variance of A over N = 100,000 Monte
Carlo samples and compares to the TRUTH formula. It does NOT test the
compiler's variance_of() — that requires the full Knowledge<f64>
chain which introduces unrelated complexities (see ζ buffer bug). The
compiler comparison is deferred to a separate test.
Pass criterion: |MC_var − 64σ²| / 64σ² < 0.05 (5% relative error).
If this passes, β's analytical formula is validated empirically. The
remaining claim — that the compiler produces 16σ² — is then a
separate reading-confirmation task.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `tuple_one_slot_struct_borrow`. &t.N / &!t.N on a tuple element that is a ONE-FIELD struct must not crash. It should compile and run successfully.
description: &t.N / &!t.N on a tuple element that is a ONE-FIELD struct must not crash
comments: tuple_borrow_elem_resolve() (fix for &t.0 / &!t.0 generally) resolves a tuple element's
address and type, but every element wider than one slot is copied inline by the tuple
constructor while a ONE-slot struct element is stored as the struct's value in rax --
a pointer to its data, not the cell holding a pointer. Taking that cell's address (as
every other element kind wants) yields a pointer to a pointer; the first read through
it dereferences garbage and segfaults.
Scope: locally built tuples only. A one-field struct inside a tuple RETURNED from a
function is its own, separate, older, pre-existing bug -- the pointer such an element
holds is into the callee's dead frame, so it is garbage after the next call whether or
not any borrow is involved (`let a = mk_one(); other_call(); a.0.n` reads garbage with
zero borrows in play). That bug is not fixed here; this test avoids it by only
constructing the one-field-struct tuples in `main`'s own frame.
Scope: local variables only (x86). Global tuple variables have a separate, pre-existing
issue with tuple-typed globals unrelated to element width, so a one-field struct in a
global tuple is not covered here either.

(closed in 2523ee2f4 by composite-type interning in lean_single.sio).
Pre-fix: ref_hash_make compounded the inner hash by *256 per level while
the inner still carried the 2^50 band, so &Option<Box<Struct>> wrapped
mod 2^64 and corrupted the struct hash — field access reported
"unknown field" and shapes collided.
Post-fix: composite inners are interned (CT_INNER_HASH[4096]) and only
a small surrogate id is multiplied, keeping the encoded hash inside
[2^50, 2^51) at arbitrary depth.
This fixture exercises field access through two structurally distinct
3-level nestings simultaneously to assert they do not alias: the same
compile unit creates and reads both &Option<Box<A>> and &Option<Box<B>>.
Under the bug, the two struct hashes would collide after the ×256 wrap
(different inner structs, same wrapped surrogate), so the field offsets
would be wrong for at least one of them.
